_doc: Timeline for build.mjs (storyboard, shot lists and tomorrow's edit: README.md). dur in seconds (rounded to 1/30). in: cut | fade (0.4 s crossfade, overlaps the previous segment). bp = where it sits in the story. Every clip or split side is a footage slot: src is the file, label what it must show, guide the in/out points; ./build.sh --slots lists them. Missing files become placeholder slates; missing cues with text become macOS 'say' placeholders (FINAL=1 refuses both, and any caption or tag still saying TBD). optional: true = left out of the final cut when its file is missing (music must not start or end on one). On a clip or a split side: ss = seconds to skip (the in point), crop = [x, y, w, h] of the source to zoom into, speed = play faster (silent; the build puts 'Sped up Nx' on screen), liveDb = keep its own sound at that gain, audioLag = read that sound this many seconds later (the VVD recorder writes it late). Overlays: {png} a card, {say, who} a spoken line burned in at the bottom, {tag} a short label at the top right; from/to in segment seconds, fade = fade time (default 0.3, 0 = none so it carries across a cut). Cue 'at' is seconds from the segment start; a cue with text is captioned while it plays; note: true also shows cards/note-synced.png.

segments.label: CLOSE-UP: the wings drawing on paper, a hand adds the last crayon stroke
segments.guide: Tonight's D1, or a kid's flyer from tomorrow if its card says wings: the same creature in every open-* slot. In: 1.4 s before the crayon lifts.

segments.label: PHONE in a hand: snaps the drawing, the cut-out appears on the checkerboard
segments.guide: In: 0.3 s before the shutter. If the cut-out needs more than 1.2 s, add "speed" (the build labels it).

segments.label: PHONE: Bring it to life! -> the card "I saw big wings -> Flies over ink blots!"
segments.guide: In: the tap on Bring it to life!. speed = (seconds from the tap to the card + 0.5) / 1.5, so the card holds for the last frames.

segments.label: VVD: the same creature pops out on the Reveal (match-cut from the phone) and starts to speak
segments.guide: capture.sh. In: 0.2 s before it pops out. The TV's own speech bubble captions its line.

segments.label: PHONE in a hand, in the race: the thumb holds TAP! (hold to run), then swipes up
segments.guide: In: as the thumb goes down. Keep the phone's race sound.

segments.label: VVD race, zoomed: the wings creature floats over an ink blot (WINGS!), a neighbour gets stunned
segments.guide: In: 0.6 s before it reaches the blot. crop to its lane, e.g. [0, 180, 1280, 720].

cues.text: What you draw changes how you play.

segments.label: KIDS at the table: hands drawing creatures with crayons (no faces)
segments.guide: Handheld, from above (runsheet 5.3). Any 7 s. Their chatter stays low under the narration.

overlays.tag: Playtest, Fri 23 Oct: TBD children aged TBD

cues.text: Kids draw on paper, and Sketchlings turns each drawing into a talking racer for the whole family.

segments.label: ROOM: phones scan the QR code on the TV, the kids' names pop into the Lobby
segments.guide: In: a phone aimed at the QR. Out: the names in the Lobby. The TV is the VVD's live view.

segments.label: PHONE in a child's hands: snaps a drawing, the cut-out with "Only this cut-out is sent"
segments.guide: In: 0.5 s before the shutter.

segments.label: PHONE close-up: the ability card "I saw <what they drew> -> <ability>"
segments.guide: Hold still 2 s: the card must be readable. Caption what the child says, or delete the say line.

segments.label: ROOM: the TV Reveal, a creature speaks in its own voice, the kids react
segments.guide: Room camera. In: 0.3 s before a creature pops out. The TV's bubble captions the creature; caption what the kids say. Only a moment where every child heard has a Voice tick; otherwise pick another or drop liveDb.

segments.label: VVD: another kid's creature on the Reveal, clean, with its voice
segments.guide: Runsheet 5.3: capture.sh kids-r1-reveal (or kids-r2-reveal). In: 0.2 s before it pops out.

segments.label: PHONE close-up in the race: a child's thumb holds TAP! to run, the phone's race sounds
segments.guide: Any 2.5 s with the thumb down and the sound audible.

overlays.tag: Hold to run · race sounds from the phone

segments.guide: One take: the best race of kids-r*-race* (point right and kids-results at it) and the handheld on the hands at the same time. Find one moment in both files (a ROAR press and its ROAR! pop) and set both ss so they start together, 17 s before the first finisher.

left.label: KIDS' hands on the phones: tap, hold, jump, ROAR

right.label: VVD: the same race, to the finish

segments.label: VVD: the podium of that race, the winner's own line
segments.guide: Same recording as the race: ss = the podium's first frame (runsheet: Results run 8 s before Enter, which is Play again).

segments.label: A child answers "Did its power help it in the race, or not? Why?" (drawing or hands in frame, no face)
segments.guide: Runsheet 5.2, question 2. Only a child with a Voice tick. Their exact words (Notes has them); an age, never a name.

segments.label: Another child, their own words about their creature or the race
segments.guide: As kids-words1 (question 1, "Tell me about your creature.", works too).

segments.label: VVD: OK on Play again, the same creatures line up for race 2
segments.guide: The next race's recording starts on the last Results: ss = 0.5 s before Enter (Play again).

segments.label: ROOM: race 2, hands on the phones, the TV behind
segments.guide: Any 4 s of race 2 with an ability pop (WINGS!, SPRINGS! ...) on the TV.

segments.label: A teacher plays for the first time: hands on a phone, their words
segments.guide: The teachers' cold test (runsheet 4), as they ticked, never a face. Their first reaction, captioned. Left out of the final if not filmed.

segments.label: A hand on a remote that really drives the VVD, the TV focus moves
segments.guide: A remote that types arrow keys and Enter into the Mac's live view (check the focus moves first), or a hand on the Mac's arrow keys (the runsheet's remote). Never a Fire TV remote as a prop: it can't drive the VVD.

overlays.tag: Remote keys reach the VVD through the live view

segments.label: VVD: Hall of Fame with today's creatures, focus moving
segments.guide: Free play (runsheet 5.5) or after: focus on the children's creatures. First visit after an app restart (notes/tv.md F11).

cues.text: Remote for menus, phones for racing, paper for creating.

segments.label: VVD: Grown-ups behind the parent gate: AI personas on/off, Clear Hall of Fame
segments.guide: Only if it ships tonight. The gate, then the two switches; don't clear the Hall.

cues.text: Behind a parent gate, grown-ups can switch AI personas off or clear the Hall of Fame.

segments.label: VVD race: WINGS! as the wings creature floats over an ink blot
segments.guide: Tonight's races. In: 1 s before the pop; crop if small. Only a creature whose card says this ability.

cues.text: Draw wings, and it floats over the ink.

segments.label: VVD race: WHEELS! on a flat stretch, the wheels creature pulls ahead
segments.guide: As ab-fly.

cues.text: Draw wheels, and it zooms on flat ground.

segments.label: VVD race: SPRINGS! as the long-legs creature jumps an ink blot
segments.guide: As ab-fly.

cues.text: Draw long legs, and it jumps higher.

segments.label: VVD race: BIG ROAR! and the ink blots ahead fly out of its lane
segments.guide: As ab-fly.

cues.text: Draw a big body, and its ROAR clears the ink.
Phones open a web page, no install. Our Bun relay links them to the TV and voices every creature with Kokoro, on a Mac at home.
Our open-source library, doodle-cutout, turns a phone photo into a clean sticker, right in the phone's browser.
Claude reads the drawing and decides how it plays. Its prompt asks for five-year-old-safe answers, and every field is checked before the TV sees it.
Engineering observations on the virtual device, not Fire TV hardware: first frame in two thirds of a second, memory well under the limit.
Races sometimes froze at the start; the crash dump showed a watchdog deadlock. After the fix, a hundred and five starts on the virtual device, zero freezes.

segments.label: YOU ON CAMERA (no live sound), or the StarFun Games logo as clips/who.png
segments.guide: Any 6.8 s. The narration carries the words. Left out of the final if not filmed.

cues.text: I'm a solo developer at StarFun Games in Sri Lanka. I built this so our screen time starts with crayons.
It's for families with kids four to ten. Little ones race with a visible speed boost. Under two cents a creature, first names only, no accounts.
